body.statement: For every fixed \(K\) for which \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) is nonempty, the rule that rejects when \(\widehat d_{\rm sp}>t_q\vert_{q=\epsilon_{\rm tot}/2}\) has total error at most \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\) against \(d(P)\ge3t_q\vert_{q=\epsilon_{\rm tot}/2}\). Uniformly over \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), therefore \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\le3t_q\vert_{q=\epsilon_{\rm tot}/2}=O(n^{-1/2})\), with the implied constant depending only on \(K\), the declared class constants, and \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\).
body.justification: The fixed-support upper bound is the mandatory attainable-rate sanity check for every growing-resolution formula.
body.gap: Existing one-NCO work gives asymptotic power without a finite-sample total-error upper bound for this constrained observed-law null.
body.consumer: Small-table applications obtain a certified root-\(n\) detectability upper bound without an unsupported matching converse.
